concern: ساعت (hour/moment) is romanised "saat", which reads as the number سات (seven) — exactly the collision ADR 0005 R5 was written to avoid (owner ruling: "saa-at", citing saat/seven as the clash to prevent). The corpus applies "saa-at" correctly elsewhere (17:? and 34:? each have one occurrence) but this verse still has the ambiguous "saat".
suggestion: Aur har giroh ke liye ek miyaad muayyan hai so jis waqt un ki miyaad muayyan aa jaayegi is waqt ek saa-at na peechhe hat sakenge aur na aage badh sakenge.

concern: دیں (gave, bare past-tense verb, fem plural agreeing with آیتیں) is romanised "din", which reads as "day" — the same collision the owner ruled on at 45:17 (Q21: write "dein", not "din"). This is the same construction, not the "kar din"/"X din" completive-auxiliary idiom used consistently elsewhere in the corpus.
suggestion: Aur un logon ko is shakhs ka haal padh kar sunaiye ke jis ko hum ne apni aayaten dein phir woh un se bilkul hi nikal gaya, phir shaitan us ke peechhe lag gaya so woh gumrah logon mein shamil ho gaya.
